concepts.label: Flush a Bucket (management operation)
concepts.reused_or_minted: minted - the operation that deletes every object a bucket contains while keeping the bucket itself, its configuration, and (per this page) any XDCR/scope/collection structure intact. Checked against the extraction-layer clusters:bucket-flush and capella:bucket-flush stubs (both minted from the Capella tree, cloud/clusters/modify-database.json and cloud/eventing/eventing-examples-high-risk.json) before minting: neither page states the Capella and Server mechanisms are the same, so kept apart per the no-silent-merge rule rather than reused.

notable_absence.finding: Unlike almost every other advanced setting in this batch (Storage Backend, Ejection Method/Policy, Encryption At Rest, Auto-Compaction), Flush is explicitly stated to apply uniformly to both bucket types: 'This setting enables or disables the Flush command for the current bucket. It can be changed at any time for all types of buckets' (edit-bucket.md, cross-referenced from this page's own Enable Flushing section). This is worth recording precisely because it is a NEGATIVE case for the round's type-gating hypothesis: not every bucket-level capability is gated by bucket type, and Flush is the clearest counter-example found in this batch.
